sessions.feedback: The data feed was fine. Two requests. (1) A read_page fallback for CNBC, Investing and Globe and Mail fetches would help; web_search content worked instead. (2) The scan tool labels the last close with the date 11-25 and shows 'gap %' against earlier closes, which is confusing after a holiday. A one-line note on which session each figure refers to would help. Nothing blocked a trade.

The economic_calendar tool still showed 08:30 ET releases (PCE, GDP) as "not out yet" about 3-5 minutes after the release time; a feed timestamp or "last updated" field would help. The digest's pre-market list is dominated by thin prints (<1% of average volume), so adding a minimum volume filter would make it more useful. Otherwise nothing blocked a trade this session.

Nothing blocked me. Two small tooling notes: web_search sometimes returns a str that must be JSON-parsed, and the scan tool's 'earnings' column helps but doesn't show beat or miss. A field with the post-earnings surprise (EPS vs consensus) in scan, or a list of today's reporters with surprise and pre-market reaction, would speed up screening for beats that did not gap.

Nothing blocked me this session. Two suggestions. (1) read_page failed on CNBC and Investing.com URLs, so I got the article text from web_search results instead; a note on which domains read_page can fetch would help. (2) A screener-style tool listing the largest idiosyncratic moves (versus industry) across all eligible stocks, including after-hours, would find catalysts faster than the digest's top-20 list, which is dominated by thin pre-market prints (100 to 1,000 shares). Stops and targets are fixed at entry, so I could not tell which stop width suits the volatility; the stop sat 0.7% below the close in a 3%-a-day tape, and I only fixed it through extend.

It is unclear whether a stop that gaps through (NVDA pre-market 141 versus a 144.88 stop) fills at the stop price or at the open price. Documenting that would help me size positions and decide whether to close manually. Otherwise nothing blocked me.

No blockers this session. Suggestions: (1) the digest's pre-market mover list is dominated by thin prints (e.g. OCSL at 200 shares), so a filter on a minimum share count or dollar volume would help. (2) The scan tool's earnings field says 'time not given' for most names, so a before-open/after-close flag would help judge whether a move already includes the earnings reaction (PANW's +9.9% regular-session move looked like earnings but came before the report). (3) A ticker-level 'consensus vs actual' feed would save web searches.

The data was sufficient. The read_page helper often returns only teasers for paywalled pages, so a way to fetch the SEC exhibit text directly would help. No blocking issues. A premarket movers list in the digest (not only previous-session movers) would help since orders fill at the open.
No VIX or futures data in tools; would help judge the volatility regime.

summary:
Session 2026-11-27.

Session 2026-11-27 (half day, pre-open). Context: 11-25 closed SPY -0.29% (716.7), QQQ -0.65% (633.9). Pre-market SPY +1.7% and QQQ +2.3%. This is a "technical" rebound in beaten-down AI names with no catalyst (worst November since 2008), and a Fed hike on 12-9 is ~99% priced. The Section 301 tariff proposal (up to 20% on China, the EU and 12 others) was published 11-25 and will not take effect for months. AS rose 2.6% that day, so it was not hurt.
Portfolio: AS held (7%, close 30.91, pre 31.15, stop 26.42, target 34.05, horizon 12-08). No company news.
New trade: long VRTX 4%. The FDA extended the povetacicept PDUFA from 11-30 to no later than 2-28-27 (a major amendment). The stock fell about 8% pre-market to 518.7, back to the 11-20 level before a 2-day run-up. JPM and Citi say not thesis-changing, and the loss of about $10B of value looks too large for a 3-month delay. Stop 7%, target 7%, 10 days, p=0.53. This is a modest edge, so I sized it small. Risks: an unknown FDA concern, and healthcare rotation unwinding into the AI bounce.
Examined, no trade: the index-level bounce (the pre-market signal has been noisy both ways); MO (-2.5% pre on a possible all-cash bid for Imperial Brands with JT, deal uncertain, deadline 12-24); VERA (+16% sympathy); PHAR (thin, not shortable); SNDK, INTC and CRWV (beta bounce). The no-chasing rule needs loosening for consumer and hardware names with clean guides: ANF closed +5.3% on 11-25 after +19.7% on 11-24, DKS +3.5%, HPQ +11.5%.
Check next session: how VRTX opens and the XLV rotation; whether QQQ holds above the 11-20 low (~596) and VIX stays below 28; CRWD 12-01, CRM 12-02, NVDA events (Huang 12-01, Senate hearing 12-03); the AS stop; FOMC 12-8/9. Cash is ~89% after VRTX.

Lessons (cite trades):
1. Beat-and-raise drift longs fail when macro beta dominates (NVDA, P, ESLT 11-17 to 11-20; ROST/INTU also sold off on beats). Do not add them while QQQ is making new lows; wait for a higher low and falling VIX. In AI hardware, even blowout beats are sold when margins are guided down (DELL, HPE 11-24/25).
2. Honour stops in a rout; do not override (NVDA: the stop saved ~11 more points). Size stops to the vol regime: with SPY moving 3-5%/day an 8-10% stop on a 4-6% daily-vol stock sits inside 2 sigma.
3. Gap risk: a stop is not a guarantee; NVDA filled -10.0% vs -9.1% stop, P -12.2% vs ~-12% planned.
4. Pre-market direction in this tape is noisy both ways (11-19 +2.1% pre then -2.2%; 11-25 -2.9% pre then -0.65%). Do not trade index pre-market moves. Cash is winning versus SPY, so cash needs a real edge to be replaced.
5. A long beats SPY only with idiosyncratic alpha; a beta bounce bet is a coin flip (about 0.5).
6. Retail earnings include IEEPA tariff-refund benefits - use adjusted numbers (LOW, WSM, TGT, ANF, HPQ).
7. Sympathy gap-ups are not trades. Thin pre-market prints (<1% of avg volume) are unreliable.
8. Merger arb: check the spread (ZS vs CRWD ~1.3%; INSM 2.4% for 6 months).
9. No-chasing rule scorecard: ANF 11-24 close 168.1 (+19.7%) vs pre +10.9%, then 11-25 close 176.96 (+5.3%); DKS 153.2 then 158.6 (+3.5%). So retail beat/raise names kept drifting up for 2 days (haven vs AI tech). URBN shows soft guides are punished hard (-12%). HPQ +11.5% on 11-25 after a pre-market read of "mixed". Lesson: when a beat has a clean guide, strength continues; the no-chasing rule is too strict for non-AI consumer/hardware names.

  news the price has not finished absorbing is a short.

  so concentrate on your best ideas. Cash is the right answer when thorough research has turned up
  nothing, and only then.
- Size positions by conviction and by how much could go wrong. Set stops and targets you would
  actually stand behind.
